EXT. [[Desert Highway]] - DAWN

A two-lane road cuts a dead-straight line through cracked hardpan. Heat shimmer already rising, and the sun is barely up.

A grey sedan sits on the shoulder, hood open, hazard lights ticking.

[[Keni]] leans over the engine block, sleeves rolled, forearms streaked with grease. He wrenches at a hose clamp. It does not move.

He straightens. He wipes his forehead with the back of his wrist, leaving a black smear.

He looks down the highway. Empty in both directions.

He pulls a phone from his pocket. No bars. He raises it above his head. Still nothing.

A distant engine note. He turns.

A tanker truck crests the rise, growing, hammering toward him. He steps into the road and waves both arms.

The truck does not slow. It blows past. The sedan rocks in the wake. Dust swallows him.

When the dust clears, Keni is still standing in the middle of the road, arms at his sides.

He walks back to the car. He slams the hood. He gets in.

INT. [[Rialto Diner]] - NIGHT

Rain hammers the windows. Neon from the sign outside bleeds red across the wet glass.

Keni sits alone in the corner booth, nursing cold coffee. His grease-streaked shirt is dry now, stiff with dust.

The door swings open. [[Mara]] steps in, soaked, scanning the room.

She spots him. She crosses the floor.

MARA
You said midnight.

KENI
I said if I could.

Mara drops a manila envelope on the table. Coffee sloshes over the rim.

Keni looks at the envelope. He does not touch it.

KENI (CONT'D)
Whose is it?

Mara slides into the booth opposite him.

MARA
Does it matter?

Keni opens the envelope. Inside, a brass key and a photograph.

He turns the photograph over. A date is written on the back in blue ink.

His jaw tightens.

KENI
This was eleven years ago.

MARA
And the unit has been paid up every month since. Somebody kept feeding it.

A waitress passes. Mara goes quiet until she is gone.

MARA (CONT'D)
Unit one fourteen. You want to know or you don't.

Keni closes his hand around the key.

EXT. [[Rialto Diner]] PARKING LOT - CONTINUOUS

Rain sheets across a half-empty lot. Puddles throw the neon back up at the sky.

Keni pushes out through the door, collar up. Mara follows.

MARA
I am not going with you.

KENI
I did not ask.

He crosses to the grey sedan. The hood is scratched where he slammed it.

Mara stops under the awning, arms folded, watching him go.

A black pickup idles at the far edge of the lot, lights off. Wipers moving. Someone is inside.

Keni does not see it. He drops into the driver's seat.

The sedan coughs, catches, pulls out onto the road.

The pickup's headlights come on.

Mara sees them. She takes a step forward.

The pickup rolls out after the sedan.

INT. [[Storage Facility]] - CORRIDOR - NIGHT

A tunnel of orange roll-up doors under buzzing strip lights. Every third bulb is dead.

Keni walks the line, checking numbers. His shoes squeak on the sealed concrete.

He stops at 114.

He crouches. He fits the brass key to the padlock. It turns.

He rolls the door up. The sound is enormous in the empty corridor.

INT. [[Storage Facility]] - UNIT 114 - CONTINUOUS

A single bulb on a pull chain. Keni yanks it.

The unit is nearly empty. One thing in the middle of the floor, under a canvas tarp, roughly the size of a chest freezer.

Keni approaches. He takes a corner of the tarp.

He pulls it off.

A wall of banker's boxes, stacked and taped, each one labeled with a year in the same blue ink.

He tears the tape on the nearest box.

Inside: hundreds of photographs, all of the same house, taken from across the street, in every season.

He picks one up. His own face is in the window.

Behind him, the corridor light goes out.

Keni turns.

INT. [[Keni]]'S CAR - MOVING - NIGHT

Rain on the windshield. Wipers at full speed and losing.

Keni drives hard, one hand on the wheel, the other holding a photograph against the steering wheel, eyes flicking down to it.

Headlights bloom in the rearview.

He checks the mirror. The black pickup is close, and closing.

He accelerates.

The pickup matches him.

Keni takes a hard right onto a service road. The sedan fishtails and recovers.

The pickup follows without slowing.

Keni's phone lights up on the passenger seat. MARA CALLING.

He reaches for it. The pickup taps his rear bumper.

The phone slides into the footwell.

EXT. [[Salt Flats]] - DAWN

The service road runs out into a white plain that goes to the horizon.

The sedan comes off the road at speed, hits the salt, and slews sideways in a long spray.

It stops. Steam pours from the hood.

Silence.

Keni sits behind the wheel, breathing hard, knuckles white.

In the mirror, the black pickup rolls to a stop a hundred yards back. It does not approach.

The driver's door opens.

A figure steps out and stands in the flat white light, too far away to read.

Keni pushes his door open. He gets out.

The two of them face each other across the salt.

The sun clears the horizon.
